column3: Is the R-factor column in Appendix C (and Table S1) the raw test value or the value normalised to C = B/2?

column7: Raw, as printed: R = M_t/(S_e F_y) at the measured C (Eq. 16, p. 29); the normalisation to C = B/2 (Sec. 4.9.2, p. 30) appears only in Figures 40-43. Carried as printed.

column3: Table 4 (insulated rotational restraint test matrix) and Table 8 (average screw location C per test) are printed as empty grids; what were their contents?

column7: Both tables are printed in the report; the page transcription missed them. Table 8 C values equal the Appendix C C column. Table 4 is the rotational-restraint (stiffness) test matrix, outside the strength database; not extracted.

column3: Each test had two parallel girts but generally only one failed; are the reported cross-section dimensions, F_y and C those of the failed girt only, and was the pressure shared equally between the two girts?

column5: All reported dimensions, F_y and C are from the failed girt only | Dimensions are averages of both girts
column6: Assume the reported S_e, F_y and C belong to the girt that failed, and that the test result represents one girt.
column7: S_e, F_y, C and t are for the failed girt (p. 21). Equal load sharing is the report's own assumption (Eq. 14: each girt carries L_p/2 = 6.79 ft). Carried as printed with a note.

column3: Because the assemblies were tested upside down, does the panel and girt self weight add to or oppose the suction-induced moment?

column5: Self weight adds to the chamber pressure effect (as in Eq. 14) | Self weight opposes it and the sign convention is approximate
column6: Assume self weight adds to the applied suction, as written in Eq. (14).
column7: Self weight adds to the suction, as written in Eq. 14 (p. 21); the assemblies were tested upside down (p. 17).

column6: Treat the reported psf as a pressure on plan area only and do not derive a per-purlin line load.
column7: 3.167 ft per purlin: 8 in. edge + half of the 5'-0" spacing, from Section 1 (Typ. @ Support Beam); 2 x 38 in. = 6'-4" sealed width. Added tributary_width_ft and failure_load_plf (psf x 3.167) to TableS1; psf kept as printed. Z 146.6/148.2, C 189.4/204.3 plf. [p4, Section 1]

column3: Back-calculating the Table 1 tested moments from the final Appendix 2 manometer readings using psf = 5.2 x reading and a 4.27 ft tributary width reproduces most tests (e.g. 5, 7, 8, 12-14, 16-20, 26, 27) but is low by a factor of about two for Tests 1-4, 9, 10, 11, 15 and 29.
